results.label: Theorem 1.1.
results.statement:
[S1.Thmtheorem1] Theorem 1.1.
 [S1.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
A compact complex surface admits at most two equivalence classes of smooth fibrations onto hyperbolic curves.

results.label: Corollary 1.2.
results.statement:
[S1.Thmtheorem2] Corollary 1.2.

results.label: Lemma 2.1.
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 2.1.
 [S2.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
If  $f:X\to B$  and  $g:X\to C$  are inequivalent smooth fibrations from a compact complex surface, then  $(f,g):X\to B\times C$  is finite and surjective.

results.label: Lemma 2.2.
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 2.2.
 [S2.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
A holomorphic line bundle on a compact curve that admits a holomorphic connection has degree zero. In particular, if a regular holomorphic foliation on a neighbourhood of a smooth compact curve  $D$  has  $D$  as a leaf, then  $\deg\mathcal{N}_{D/X}=0$ .

results.label: Lemma 2.3.
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem3] Lemma 2.3.
 [S2.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
Let  $u:D\to B$  and  $v:D\to C$  be nonconstant maps of curves, with  $g(B),g(C)\geq 2$ . If their ramification divisors on  $D$  coincide, then  $u^{*}h_{B}=v^{*}h_{C}$ . Near every point of  $D$ , the image of  $(u,v)$  is contained in the graph of a holomorphic local hyperbolic isometry from  $B$  to  $C$ .

results.label: Proposition 2.4.
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem4] Proposition 2.4.
 [S2.Thmtheorem4.p1] 
Let  $f:X\to B$  and  $g:X\to C$  be inequivalent smooth fibrations from a compact complex surface to hyperbolic curves. The reduced support of  $R(f,g)$  is a disjoint union of smooth compact curves  $D$ , and  $f|_{D}$  and  $g|_{D}$  are unramified coverings. If  $D$  has coefficient  $n-1$  in  $R(f,g)$ , then  $n\geq 2$  and
 [S2.E1] 
 $\mathcal{N}_{D/X}^{\otimes n}\cong TD,\qquad D^{2}=-\frac{2g(D)-2}{n}<0.$ (1)

There is a neighbourhood  $U$  of  $D$  on which  $f$  and  $g$  lift to holomorphic retractions  $r,s:U\to D$ . Moreover,  $U$  admits a cyclic action of order  $n$  fixing  $D$  pointwise and preserving  $r$  and  $s$ . Locally along  $D$ , suitable coordinates give
 [S2.E2] 
 $r=x,\qquad s=x+y^{n},\qquad\tau(x,y)=(x,\zeta y),\qquad\zeta=e^{2\pi i/n}.$ (2)

Here the same coordinate on  $D$  is used for both retractions.

results.label: Remark 2.5 (Checking both projections).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem5] Remark 2.5 (Checking both projections).
 [S2.Thmtheorem5.p1] 
A branched cover which gives one smooth fibration need not give a second. For a cyclic cover branched along a smooth graph  $z=\phi(t)$ , the local map is
 [S2.Ex10] 
 $(t,w)\longmapsto(t,w^{m}+\phi(t)),\qquad m\geq 2.$ 

The first projection is a submersion. The differential of the second is  $mw^{m-1}\mathrm{d}w+\phi^{\prime}(t)\mathrm{d}t$ , which vanishes at a ramification point with  $\phi^{\prime}(t)=0$ .

 [S2.Thmtheorem5.p2] 
This distinction matters for the branch-cover construction discussed in [4, Remark 2.6], where the branch divisor is étale over one factor but ramified over the other. In the intermediate genus-six family of [10, pp. 186–187], a genus-nine curve  $F$  has degree-two maps  $\pi_{i}:F\to C_{3}$  to a genus-three curve. After an unramified base change  $B\to F$ , the family is a double cover of  $B\times C_{3}$  branched along the two resulting graphs. Hurwitz’s formula gives
 [S2.Ex11] 
 $\deg\divisor(\mathrm{d}\pi_{i})=(2\cdot 9-2)-2(2\cdot 3-2)=8.$ 

This ramification persists under the unramified base change, and the local calculation above shows that the projection of this intermediate family to  $C_{3}$  is not a submersion. The construction therefore does not supply two smooth projections. This observation concerns the intermediate family, not Zaal’s subsequent construction of a family of genus-three curves.

results.label: Lemma 3.1.
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 3.1.
 [S3.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
Let  $D$  be a component of  $R_{12}$ . Either  $D\cap(R_{13}\cup R_{23})=\varnothing$ , or  $D$  is a component of all three divisors. In the latter case its ramification index is the same for all three pairs.

results.label: Lemma 3.2.
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 3.2.
 [S3.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
The disjoint alternative in Lemma 3.1 is impossible.

results.label: Lemma 3.3.
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem3] Lemma 3.3.
 [S3.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
The common-component alternative in Lemma 3.1 is impossible.

results.label: Lemma 3.4.
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem4] Lemma 3.4.
 [S3.Thmtheorem4.p1] 
Let  $q:X\to B_{1}\times B_{2}$  be a finite unramified covering, with  $g(B_{1}),g(B_{2})\geq 2$ . Suppose the induced factor maps  $f_{i}=\operatorname{pr}_{i}\circ q$  have connected fibres. Every fibration  $h:X\to C$  onto a hyperbolic curve is then equivalent to  $f_{1}$  or  $f_{2}$ .
